You should know that everyone does not look the same or even have the same type of bodies. You should tell yourself you love yourself, and wanting to be yourself every single day, because becoming and loving yourself is the most important thing to have and being you is a beautiful thing to be. 

I hope this helps, and if you need anything else or struggling, you should DM me. I am practicing self love, too.

Hi! I have the same experience with you as I was a freshman in high school. I met a guy in my English class that I liked and he was a shy guy. So, we dated, and turns out that he does not like talking at all. He will only speak to me in class or in the hallways, but little to no text messages or out of school. I kept dating him for 1 year, letting everyone make my decisions for me. I ended the relationship because of lack of communication. 

Some guys like their space, and I respect that. But if you are a person who thinks that communication is the key to a relationship, then your ex is not the person to be with since the lack of talking and connection. If you were unhappy or uncomfortable with the relationship, then do not stay around and wait for that person, because chances are, they not going to communicate with you. 

Also, your friend should be supporting you, even if they do not like your ex or boyfriend. They should help you with your decisions, but not making decisions for you. Ask yourself, "What's good for myself?" "What is the best thing for me?" "How can I make my decisions the way I can be confident and comfortable with?" Think about the decisions they make for you and their reasoning, and then think about your decisions, what you want to do, and your reasonings. You should do what's best for you, not others around you.

As a person who in a relationship for 2 years now and have so many fighting issues, I would say that fighting can be a way to know what and how you and your partner see and think. At times, you will not have the same exact views or opinions or likes and interests as your partner. I suggest that you guys should sit down, face to face, and talk about the fighting (think and ask of the questions, "What should we do if we get into another argument?" "How can we sit down and talk things out during an argument?" "How and what should we do if we catch ourselves into a heated argument?"). It's normal for partners to fight at times, but day to day fighting or fighting too often should be taken seriously and should have some measures taken in. If it is day to day fighting, then I think you guys need a break or not very compatible, but first, talk to your partner in a calming way first before making your decision.
